A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MegaRAG. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original global and local question-answering experiments, component ablations, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multimodal baseline comparisons, evaluator comparisons, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The pagewise MMKG construction, subgraph-assisted refinement, GME indexing, graph/page retrieval, and two-stage answer generation remain unchanged. The appendix construction and generation prompts are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four UltraDomain subsets, four multimodal global-QA collections, SlideVQA (2k), and four RealMMBench subsets. Dataset statistics are unchanged between v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 7. Added comparisons use existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported head-to-head comparisons with VisRAG, GME, and ColQwen on four multimodal collections (Table 4), plus Query-driven MMKG on World History and Environmental Report (Table 10). v1 discussed several of these methods but did not evaluate them as these comparators. Existing baselines remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds supplementary evaluation using Gemini-3-Flash and indexing/latency measurement procedures. Existing dataset sizes, generation models, retrieval budgets, and primary metrics remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 newly describes swapped-answer-order evaluation and tie handling, but does not establish that the retained main-result experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds evaluator-bias and judge-sensitivity analysis (Appendix C.3) and computational overhead analysis (Section 4.7). Conversely, the component-ablation table contracts from four datasets to two; Environmental Report and GenAI A2/A3 results disappear. The retrieval-free GPT-4o-mini ablation and existing case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2 first reports inter-judge agreement, giving Cohen's kappa of 0.72 on winning samples in Appendix C.3. v1 reports no corresponding agreement statistic. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-seed uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their original scores, including 64.85% SlideVQA accuracy. v2 adds substantial result blocks for multimodal comparators, a second judge, Query-driven MMKG, and computational costs; it reports approximately 42 seconds per question versus GME's 26.4 seconds. Some component-ablation results are removed. These additions do not establish improved performance over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The graph definitions and construction/refinement equations are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The central automatic-MMKG, refinement, and global/local-QA contributions remain. However, v2 removes v1's categorical claim to be the first automatic MMKG approach for multimodal RAG in Section 4.2 and acknowledges automatic MMKG prior work in Section 2, narrowing the novelty claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning cross-document QA, multimodal dataset scale, treating each figure as one entity, and propagation of extraction hallucinations. It also discusses computational tradeoffs and evaluator stability, and qualifies the Query-driven comparison through differing operating regimes and best-effort reproduction.

D1.justification: v2 documents timing breakdowns and measurement conditions, answer-order swapping and its tie rule, and missing extraction-prompt details in the Query-driven reproduction. Existing implementation prompts, hyperparameters, and encoder hardware information remain. The expanded printed code URL points to the same repository already linked in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bu et al. (2025), Query-driven multimodal GraphRAG, and distinguishes its online query-specific graphs from MegaRAG's offline document-level construction and refinement. This is a focused revision of positioning relative to a close predecessor; the remaining cited literature is retained.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the evaluation, implementation, and ablation prose, updates affiliations, and inserts comparison, overhead, limitations, ethics, and appendix subsections. Most of the introduction, methodology, conclusion, prompts, and case-study text retains its wording and organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive tables for multimodal comparisons, construction costs, judge comparisons, and Query-driven MMKG results. It restructures the ablation display to two datasets and compresses the local-QA table into a smaller single-column display. Existing appendix figures and case-study tables are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added multimodal comparisons, evaluator checks, cost reporting, and explicit limitations address important gaps in v1. However, the new GME rows exactly match v1's text-only-graph ablation scores without explanation, and Table 9 reports 81.0% for MegaRAG's World History Empowerment result against GraphRAG while retained Table 2 reports 96.0%. Component-ablation coverage also contracts. These attribution and consistency problems leave the reliability of some added validation, and therefore the net quality improvement, uncertain.
